But that's not the same as saying "donating to all charity is negative." He just wants to make the decision for himself, rather than deferring to a foundation staffed by nonprofit drones.

If you're looking for a "don't donate to charity" clip, or even a "billionaires are evil" clip, you picked the wrong one.

The psychology of every “we’re so back” cycle:

Majors pump.

↓

Shorts get liquidated. The squeeze sends prices higher.

↓

Prices keep climbing. Confidence slowly returns.

↓

Trading picks up. People start posting PnLs again.

↓

The feed starts filling with everyone winning. Being sidelined starts hurting.

↓

FOMO kicks in. Sideliners start buying.

↓

Profits from majors flow into riskier assets and leveraged longs.

↓

Bigger wins, more PnL sharing, more people chasing.

↓

Winning feels easy. Leverage amounts progress.

↓

Everyone raises their targets instead of taking profits.

↓

The first dump gets bought. The bounce brings another wave of FOMO.

↓

More shorts get liquidated. Bears are fcked. Bulls are in control.

↓

The next dip barely bounces. Trading gets harder.

↓

Overleveraged longs get liquidated. Forced selling triggers more liquidations.

↓

PnL screenshots are getting rarer. It's now liquidation data.

↓

FOMO flips from fear of missing gains to fear of losing what’s left.

↓

Everyone turns bearish again.

$SIVE ER transcript just dropped, TLDR:

- 6 NEW pluggable players working with Sivers now.

Probably the biggest news of the entire ER next to new foundry allocations. 

"3 are in alpha sample evaluation stage" and another 3 in technical engagement / supply assessment stage."

And now it makes more sense why their $1.2B revenue pipeline ballooned (since this was a bigger leap than Jabil). 

- Initial production orders with $JBL expected in the first half of 2027, with the production ramp planned second half of 2027

LFG, Jabil is a massive hyperscaler supplier and finally got clear timelines on revenue from volume ramp.

- "new foundry partner who has brought on tremendous capacity that is available now"

This is what I wanted to hear. Apparently they've been in the works for this for awhile since it's "available now", and THIS IS VERY MATERIAL. 

CW lasers are in a massive shortage and $SIVE brought on new supply outside of Win Semi (also de-risks).

As you hear with other qualified CW players (anything they make gets sold), so as Sivers partners finishes their qualifications, I'm expecting the same.

- "long-term capacity model where one-third of manufacturing capacity will be internal, while two-thirds will come from our foundry partners"

Lukewarm on this, it makes sense they need to be vertically integrated like $AAOI / $LITE eventually but implies more capex (better after NASDAQ listing).

As you see with ESMT + DDR2 bottlenecks, the operating income they get from just securing wafers during shortages and doing fabless models is incredible. 

And it would make more sense to fund this with cashflow down the road.

- NASDAQ listing ongoing. CFO gave a very lawyer like answer, but on track as usual.

- "We do not see production capacity as a bottleneck at this point in time"

This is very meaningful since with their new foundry partners, implies $SIVE is coming online with a very material CW laser supply to a bottlenecked market.

TLDR:
- NEW substantial FOUNDRY ALLOCATION! (very, very material during CW laser shortage)
- 6 new pluggable players outside of $JBL 
- Clear revenue ramp timelines from Jabil

Heavy focus on pluggables -> NPO -> CPO seems like the progression.  Only lukewarm piece was building up internal capacity but it's long term positive.  

Anyway, very happy after reading the transcript aside from potential capex prioritizing laser capacity (which is fine too during an industry shortage) over IP acquisition.

The 6 new pluggable players + substantial wafer allocation "available now" is a pretty insane disclosure.

China can already run competitive AI models on domestic hardware, but it still has not demonstrated a frontier-scale training run using a fully domestic stack.

Frontier training requires thousands of accelerators to work together reliably at scale. That coordination depends on fast connections between chips, sufficient memory and stable software. A weakness anywhere in the system can stop the run.

China still relies on Nvidia stockpiles and approved imports for frontier training while Huawei develops domestic infrastructure around Ascend. Bringing that infrastructure to scale will also require more chip output from SMIC and continued progress in domestic memory and networking.

The 2027–28 model generation is the first that could plausibly be trained on Huawei’s domestic infrastructure. A fully disclosed training run would confirm that China can train frontier models without foreign hardware.

If I could ask @danroberts0101 one question after tonight's call, it would be --->

You said 100% of IREN’s DC portfolio remains unencumbered and mentioned refinancing Horizons 1–4 once stabilized.

IREN’s vertical integration is truly novel. Other DC owners are borrowing against long-term leases to hyperscalers and neoclouds. IREN is both the DC owner and the neocloud, but the GPU financing is already secured by the chips and the Microsoft cash flows.

Assuming Horizons can sit in a property SPV with an intercompany lease (or is there another structure you prefer?) how different would its financing terms be versus a traditional DC with a third-party hyperscaler/neocloud lease? Is the difference mainly rate or leverage, or both? How much does waiting for stabilization close that gap?

This is a huge variable for shareholders. Horizons is ~$3B of DC investment. Refinancing most of that could recycle capital equivalent to ~79M shares at $38, or ~20% of today's share count.

After tonight’s call, the market sees a ~$5.5B funding gap: $27.5B of capex minus $14B already secured minus ~$8B of targeted GPU financing/prepayments.

If you can pull this off an attractive Horizons refi and repeat it across the portfolio, equity needs plummet.

Misleading. 

Georgia froze residential base rates through 2028, with data-center growth a key reason it could do so. Georgia Power now says large loads, including the new OpenAI deal, will save a typical household at least $180/year starting in 2029, up from $102 previously. 

Yes there is a real issue with big customers on real-time pricing pushing some hedging and pipeline costs onto household fuel bills. Regulators are looking at it.

But the estimated hit from those factors is $23–50/year per household, versus the $180/year in projected savings from large loads. Seems pretty clear that the net result is better for household ratepayers.

And the really big costs, the new plants and wires needed to serve data centers, are walled off by contracts that make these large customers pay for them.

An invisible economy is coming, and all of it inevitably happens onchain. DeFi is the obvious venue.

The Blokyz team brought me on to audit their contract, and when they asked me to be a signer on the multisig, I happily obliged.

2/3 multisig does not make the project rug-proof, but it does mean that any contract actions (like setting the raffle root, refundTotal, or withdrawing the proceeds) must be approved by myself or SimpleFarmer, in addition to the Blokyz team.

As for raffle fairness - the selection mechanism has already been finalized, and a hash of the file has been stored on the contract in advance (allocatorHash is set to 0x248c357ef216602dfb5381b5e1f680a6a5b002c39f620f9ec9e054b6bf08ca22).

Post raffle, the allocation script will be made public and anybody can verify that the script used matches the stored hash, and also produces the raffle results used by the team.

This does not reduce the centralization risk, but does hold the team accountable in retrospect: if anything was manipulated, it is easy to prove publicly.

I audit a lot of projects and my audits should never be seen as an endorsement of a protocol/project, but as it pertains to the workings of the contract itself, I am always happy to step in and clear things up.

Good luck.
